answers.answer: Under AS/NZS 3500.2:2021 Clause 4.6.5, where a disconnector gully is located inside a building, the vent pipe branching from the riser pipe (or a fitting) must be DN 50 — i.e. the minimum nominal size of the vent pipe is DN 50. Clause 4.6.5(b) states: "a DN 50 vent pipe, branching from the riser pipe or a fitting, extends at a grade of not less than 1.25 % and terminates with a grating at an external wall of the building". The pipe must terminate (i) above the overflow level of the lowest internal fixture connected to the sealed disconnector gully, (ii) at least 75 mm above finished surface level, and (iii) in areas likely to be inundated, per Clause 4.6.6.8. Fixtures/appliances must not connect to the vent pipe (4.6.5(c)), and air admittance valves must not be used to vent sealed disconnector gullies (4.6.5(d)).

answers.answer: Concrete pads used to support drains shall be a minimum of 100 mm thick. The library states: "Concrete pads used to support drains shall be a minimum of 100 mm thick and be laid — (a) under gully traps and boundary traps of material other than cast iron; (b) under all inspection junctions where a riser is brought to the surface; (c) under all bends greater than DN 65 forming risers from the main drain; (d) not closer than 20 mm to flexible joints; (e) for square junctions, beneath the junction to a minimum thickness of 100 mm and continued up vertically to the centre of the junction fitting; and (f) for 45° junctions, beneath the junction to a minimum thickness of 100 mm and continued up vertically to the underside of the bend fitted to the junction fitting." Note also Clause 4.4.4.1(c), which requires a concrete pad under boundary traps of material other than cast iron of not less than 100 mm thick, and Clause 4.4.3.1(d), which requires a concrete footing not less than 100 mm thick under a jump-up bend. This edition is the published AS/NZS 3500.2:2021 (not marked superseded in the excerpts; note house rule that a 2025 edition was published 2025-04-17 — the library holds 2021).

answers.answer: Under AS/NZS 3500.2:2021, Clause 6.6.2.4.2 (New installations), where a junction is used to connect a DN 100 branch pipe to another DN 100 pipe, the entry level of the branch pipe shall be elevated at an incline of not less than 15° above the horizontal. The clause states: "Where a junction is used to make the connection of a DN 100 branch pipe to another DN 100 pipe, the entry level of the branch pipe shall be elevated at an incline of not less than 15° above the horizontal." NOTE 2 explains that positioning the junction a minimum of 15° above horizontal removes the probability of partial backwash causing stranding that can lead to blockages.

answers.answer: For a DN 100 stack serving the first floor above ground level in a domestic or residential building, with the top (graded) section receiving discharge from fixtures whose discharge pipes are unvented, Clause 9.8.5 permits this provided, among other things, that the stack loading does not exceed 90 fixture units. The same limit is confirmed in Clause 9.8.1(d), which describes 'A DN 100 stack of one floor in height with top section graded (nominally horizontal), receiving a maximum discharge of 90 fixture units', and in Figure 9.8.5, titled 'Typical DN 100 stack with topmost section nominally horizontal for one floor — 90 fixture units'. Note the distinction from Clause 9.8.4 (DN 100, up to three floor levels, top section graded) which is limited to 30 fixture units. Other conditions of Clause 9.8.5 also apply: fixtures discharge to the graded section by individual fixture discharge pipes (see Table 9.5.1), fixture discharge pipe connections to the graded section are not less than 450 mm from the lower vertical section of the stack, and branches are not connected to the vertical section within 600 mm below the lower bend forming the offset.

answers.answer: Under AS/NZS 3500.2:2021, Clause 16.15.2 (Vacuum test pressure) sets an initial vacuum test pressure of −55 ± 5 kPa applied to the section being tested. answers.answer: Under AS/NZS 3500.2:2021 Clause 16.15 (Vacuum test for vacuum drainage systems), all vacuum sanitary plumbing and drainage inlets, outlets and access openings must first be capped and sealed. An initial vacuum test pressure of −55 ± 5 kPa must then be applied to the section being tested. When −55 ± 5 kPa is reached, the vacuum pump and supply valve are shut off, and the vacuum is allowed to stabilize for a minimum of 3 min while checking for leaks. (The test then continues by allowing the vacuum to fall to −50 kPa and recording the drop over the minimum test duration in Table 16.15.3.) Note: the Section 15.4 vacuum test at approximately 15 kPa applies to general sanitary plumbing and drainage installations, not to dedicated vacuum drainage systems.

answers.answer: The library text for trench fill is in Clause 6.2.10 (Trench fill), and the sentence carrying the two limits runs under the 6.2.11 (Backfilling) heading on p.83 of AS/NZS 3500.3:2021: 'Trench fill shall be placed in loose layers not more than 200 mm thick and compacted to not less than 90 % or 95 % under pavements of the standard maximum dry density specified in AS 1289.5.4.1 or AS 1289.5.6.1'. So the maximum loose layer thickness is 200 mm, and under pavements the minimum compaction is 95 % of the standard maximum dry density (with 90 % expressed as the general figure for other locations). Note the question asks about 'Clause 6.2.11': in this edition 6.2.11 is titled 'Backfilling' and its heading sits between the loose-layer/compaction sentence, so the requirement is read from that text at p.83. Clause 2.11 (p.23) simply refers trench fill to Clause 6.2.10.
values: 95 % under pavements (90 % otherwise) of standard maximum dry density per AS 1289.5.4.1 or AS 1289.5.6.1

answers.answer: For an in-situ rectangular brickwork stormwater pit, Clause 7.5.5.1(a)(i) requires a wall depth measured from the existing surface to the invert of the outlet that does not exceed 600 mm to be 110 mm minimum thick. A 500 mm wall depth falls within that band, so the minimum wall thickness is 110 mm. The library text states: "Brickwork for wall depths, measured from the existing surface to the invert of the outlet, that — (A) do not exceed 600 mm, 110 mm min. thick; or (B) exceed 600 mm but not 1 500 mm, 230 mm min. thick." The pit must also be constructed in situ on a 150 mm min. thick concrete bed with at least the same external dimensions as the pit.

answers.answer: Under AS/NZS 3500.3:2021, Clause 9.3 — Test criteria requires downpipes within buildings to be free of leaks when subjected to either a water test OR an air test. Clause 9.3.1(b) — Downpipes within buildings states that the air test must be at a pressure of not less than 30 kPa for a period of not less than 3 min. The water test in Clause 9.3.1(a) is a head of water equal to the lesser of 10 m or the length of the downpipe held for not less than 10 min. Note that clause 9.3.1(b) contains no pressure-drop criterion for downpipes within buildings — the 25 kPa→20 kPa drop timing in the air test procedure (Clause 9.4.2, Tables 9.3.2(B)) is intended for site stormwater drains and drains within/under buildings per Clause 9.3.2(b).
values: Water test (alternative): head of water equal to the lesser of 10 m or length of downpipe for not less than 10 min

answers.answer: Under AS/NZS 3500.1:2018 Clause 5.2.10, a water service pipe must be installed with sufficient clearance to any underground obstruction to protect it from physical damage and permit repairs. The clearance must be at least 100 mm for a water service not exceeding DN 65 — so a DN 50 pipe requires a minimum clearance of 100 mm. (300 mm applies only where the pipe exceeds DN 65.) Note: the 2018 edition held in the library is marked superseded; the equivalent current provision in the held 2021 edition is Clause 5.3.5, which gives the same 100 mm / 300 mm figures.
values: 100 mm (water service not exceeding DN 65, i.e. DN 50)
300 mm (only for water service exceeding DN 65 — not applicable to DN 50)

answers.answer: Under AS/NZS 3500.1:2018, Clause 8.4.1 (General, Tank design), where the capacity of the water storage tank exceeds 500 L, provision shall be made at the base for removal of sludge. So provision is required for tanks with a capacity above 500 L. (Clause 8.7—Sludge valves—is consistent: a sludge valve shall be fitted where the capacity of the tank exceeds 500 L, with minimum size not less than half the outlet pipe size nor less than DN 40.) Note: the 2018 edition is superseded; the AS/NZS 3500.1:2021 edition in the library carries the same requirement in Clause 8.4.1 (p.70).

answers.answer: Under AS/NZS 3500.2:2018 the maximum length depends on the fixture, but for every untrapped fixture discharging to a floor waste gully riser the Table 4.6.7.2 figure is 1.2 m (the only untrapped exception listed is a tundish at 10.0 m, and discharge to a submerged-inlet floor waste gully is not allowed for untrapped fixtures). Clause 4.6.7.3 requires each fixture connected to a floor waste gully to be connected by a separate waste pipe at a grade not less than 2.5% and with a length not exceeding that specified in Table 4.6.7.2. Appendix B likewise gives "Untrapped DN 40 waste 1.2" and "Untrapped DN 50 waste 1.2" against the floor waste gully column. Note the excerpt is from a superseded edition (edition_status: superseded).
values: 1.2 m (maximum length of untrapped waste pipe to floor waste gully riser, per Table 4.6.7.2)

answers.answer: Under AS/NZS 3500.2:2018 Clause 6.8.1(b), for stacks of two floor levels or less, no connection shall be made closer than 500 mm upstream (or downstream) of the base of the stack. In addition, Clause 6.8.1(b)(ii) requires that no discharge pipe connecting a fixture upstream of a junction that connects a stack to a drain or graded pipe shall be within 500 mm of the base of the stack. So the minimum upstream distance is 500 mm. Note: the library's held edition (2018) is marked superseded, and AS/NZS 3500.2:2021 is the edition in this library's Library facts listing as latest held only for the 2021 set — the excerpt itself is tagged edition_status: superseded, so confirm against the current edition.

answers.answer: Under AS/NZS 3500.2:2018, Clause 9.5.11.2, the fixture discharge pipe from each basin to the point of connection to the common discharge pipe shall be not longer than 1 m. answers.answer: Under AS/NZS 3500.2:2018 Clause 9.9.5 (graded offsets), a DN 100 stack may be offset between the base of the stack and the highest connection, but only where one graded offset is installed and "The height of the stack shall not exceed 10 consecutive floor levels." So the maximum is 10 consecutive floor levels. Note that the edition quoted is superseded. Also note that the separate rule in Clause 9.9.6(a) limits the vertical section above the upper offset bend to 5 consecutive floor levels — a different limit applying to connections above the offset.

answers.answer: For a holding tank under AS/NZS 3500.2:2018 Clause 12.8 (pumping discharge from waste fixtures), Clause 12.8.6 'Venting' requires the holding tank to be provided with a vent having a minimum size of DN 50, conforming to the venting requirements for waste fixtures, and positioned a minimum of 100 mm above the waste inlet. (Note: this differs from a wet well under Clause 12.6.3, which requires a minimum DN 80 vent.) The excerpt library holds AS/NZS 3500.2:2018 as a superseded edition (edition_status: superseded); the current edition should be checked.

answers.answer: No — the figure is 300 mm, not 900 mm. The library contradicts the premise in the question. The same 300 mm minimum applies to SPVBs under Clause 4.6.3.2(g)(i), and Figure 7.2(D) on p.66 also shows the pressure type vacuum breaker at '300 min. above highest sprinkler head'. (For contrast, the 150 mm minimum applies to atmospheric vacuum breakers under Clause 4.6.3.3(a)(i).) No 900 mm requirement appears for a PVB in the excerpts.
